correctness.rationale: All 4095 nonzero bidegree-(2,3) forms were checked on four affine charts by exact binary Jacobian ideals: 1116 were geometrically smooth; all 2,794,155 pencils are represented uniquely by triples {a,b,a xor b}. Enumeration gives 44,070 qualifying pencils. A separately implemented SymPy Gröbner test agreed with each smoothness flag. An additive Fourier/Walsh approach independently reproduces 44,070 and the rational-point binomial moments, yielding counts 6066, 16884, 17424, 3696. Complete orbit generation under 36 coordinate automorphisms gives 1242 orbits, frequencies 1,3,30,1208 for sizes 6,12,18,36; catalogue and executable proofs are bundled. No finite experiment is used to claim an infinite statement.

value.rationale: A bidegree (2,3) divisor on the split quadric is a natural genus-two model and fully smooth pencils are intrinsic to finite-field Bertini questions. This exact smallest-field simultaneous-smoothness census, complete projective orbit stratification, and rational-base-point incidence profile determine natural geometric/arithmetic invariants not obtained from the count of individual curves; genus-two moduli and fiber smoothness motivate the problem independently of its numerical answer.
